original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Batch immutable Git source reads in registered-package metadata validation while rechecking every pin and live input on each invocation.
scope_change_reason: The selected runtime card is narrowed to the metadata stage of opt-in research replay. Reuse is only a per-invocation Git transport; no successful proof/validation result or live bytes are cached. This is verifier throughput tooling, not a selected-circuit optimization.
bottleneck_link: Fewer Git startup costs make independently reviewable source-bound packages cheaper to validate. Mathematical command coverage, input invalidation and the selected frontier are unchanged.
stop_rule: One implementation and one fixed 34-source fixture; seven alternating benchmark pairs, exact decision equivalence, source-drift and malformed-protocol controls. Stop if exact checks cannot be preserved or if no measurable gain remains.
evidence: Seven alternating-order benchmark pairs: 1.928127s to 0.073139s median (26.36x) on the identical 34-source fixture. All nine validation rejection controls and seven focused transport tests pass, including eight malformed responses, fresh live bytes and child cleanup. Metadata and selected source-binding checks pass. Windows timeout failure independently reproduced with exact original implementation; Python 3.12 and Linux replay remain unrun.
author: Arham Tahir
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in design, implementation, tests, measurement and writing; no independent human or subagent review.

open_questions.question: How much does batched validation save on large real contributed manifests on Linux CI?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The controlled local fixture isolates Git process overhead but cannot predict all platforms, pack layouts or complete replay timings.
open_questions.first_step: Run this identical-fixture benchmark on Linux and compare full package metadata validation on one accepted large manifest.
open_questions.blocked_by: Requires representative accepted manifests and hosted measurements; no timing threshold should be used for mathematical acceptance.

selected_method: Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
concrete_object: scripts/research_package.py validate(check_pins=True), exact base source and fixed 34-source fixture
method_domain: Literal NUL-delimited Git tree lookup plus one streaming cat-file process; arbitrary blob bytes; all pin rows, including duplicate IDs. No persistent cache.
expected_improvement: Reduce 2N+1 Git processes to two for N source pins; preserve acceptance/rejection and strict live byte equality.

coordination.coverage: Connected GitHub REST read paginated 718 open-PR rows across pages 1..8 (page 9 empty); public active Discussion list and coordination threads read. Discussion comment pagination and code-diff search were not complete. No match is not proof of novelty.
